title: Sherlock Holmes: A Study in Scarlet — Ep 09/14 — "The Flower of Utah"
description:
A Study in Scarlet, Episode 9. Twelve years on from the desert, and John Ferrier is the richest farmer in Salt Lake City.

The child he carried out of the alkali is nineteen now, and she rides her father's mustang into the city on his business as she has a hundred times before. It is a warm June morning; the gold fever has broken out west and the road to it runs through the City of the Elect, so the way in is full of mules and immigrant waggons and men going somewhere else.

At the outskirts the road is stopped bank to bank by a drove of long-horned cattle. She sees a gap and puts her horse into it, and the beasts close up behind her.

A horn comes round and strikes the mustang in the flank.

What happens next takes about four seconds and decides the rest of her life, and the rest of several other people's. A sinewy brown hand catches the bridle; the man on the roan is clad in the rough dress of a hunter with a long rifle slung over his shoulders, and he would like to know whether her father remembers the Jefferson Hopes of St. Louis.

By midsummer her heart is no longer her own. And there is a promise made at a gate at sundown, with two months on it.

Chapter II of Part Two of Arthur Conan Doyle's A Study in Scarlet (1887), in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
